concepts.title: Physical Properties of Metals
concepts.definition: Metals are elements characterized by their ability to shine, be hammered into sheets, drawn into wires, and conduct both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both heat and electricity.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Metals are generally hard, lustrous, malleable, ductile, and sonorous solids.
question_patterns: What are the physical properties of metals?
Define malleability and ductility in metals.
Why are metals used to make bells?
Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
Explain why copper is used for electrical wiring.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the substance is lustrous, malleable, or ductile.
Confirm if it is solid at room temperature and conducts electricity.

concepts.title: Amphoteric Oxides
concepts.definition: Metal oxides that exhibit both acidic and basic behavior by reacting with both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both acids and bases to yield salt and water.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Dual-nature oxides like aluminium both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both oxide and zinc oxide react with both H+ and OH- ions.
question_patterns: What are amphoteric oxides?
Give two examples of amphoteric oxides.
Show how aluminium oxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.
Explain the dual nature of zinc oxide.

solution_steps.explain: The oxide reacts with HCl to form a metal chloride and water.
The oxide reacts with NaOH to form a salt (like sodium aluminate) and water.

concepts.title: Metal Reactivity with Water
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the process where metals react with water to produce metal oxides or hydroxides and release hydrogen gas.
concepts.key_idea: Reactivity varies from violent (sodium) to no reaction (gold) based on the metal's position in the series.
question_patterns: How does sodium react with cold water?
Why does calcium float on water during a reaction?
Which metals react only with steam?
Write the equation for iron reacting with steam.

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the metal reacts with cold water, hot water, or steam.
Highly reactive metals form hydroxides; moderately reactive ones form oxides.

concepts.title: The Reactivity Series
concepts.definition: A ranking of metals in descending order of their chemical activity, primarily based on displacement reactions.
concepts.formula: A + BC -> AC + B (if A is more reactive than B)
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, More reactive metals displace less reactive ones from their salt solutions.
question_patterns: What is the reactivity series?
Predict if zinc will displace iron from iron sulphate.
Arrange Mg, Al, Zn, and Fe in decreasing order of reactivity.
Why is gold found in its native state?

solution_steps.explain: Check the relative positions of the two metals in the activity series.
If the standalone metal is higher in the series, displacement occurs.

concepts.title: Properties of Ionic Compounds
concepts.definition: Compounds formed by the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions created through electron transfer.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Ionic compounds have indeed high melting points and conduct electricity when molten or dissolved.
question_patterns: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
Explain the electrical conductivity of NaCl in water.
Describe the physical nature of electrovalent compounds.
Why don't ionic solids conduct electricity?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the strong electrostatic forces between cations and anions.
High energy is needed to break the lattice, leading to high melting points.

concepts.title: Roasting and Calcination
concepts.definition: In brief, thermal processes to convert ores into metal oxides: roasting involves excess air for sulphides, while calcination uses limited air for carbonates.
concepts.key_idea: Oxides are easier to reduce to pure metals than sulphides or carbonates.
question_patterns: Distinguish between roasting and calcination.
How is zinc extracted from its carbonate ore?
Write the reaction for roasting of cinnabar.
Why are ores converted to oxides before reduction?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the ore is a sulphide or a carbonate.
Apply roasting for sulphides (with O2) or calcination for carbonates (limited O2).

concepts.title: Electrolytic Refining
concepts.definition: A method of purifying metals using electrolysis where the impure metal is indeed the anode and pure metal is the cathode.
concepts.key_idea: Pure metal transfers from the anode to the cathode through an electrolyte solution.
question_patterns: Describe the electrolytic refining of copper.
What is anode mud?
In refining, which electrode is made of pure metal?
What electrolyte is used for refining zinc?

solution_steps.explain: Place impure metal at the anode and pure strip at the cathode.
Metal ions dissolve from anode and deposit on cathode.

concepts.title: Gold Purity Calculation
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, Calculating the percentage of pure gold in an alloy using its carat rating, where 24 carats represents 100% purity.
concepts.key_idea: Carat measures the parts of gold out of 24 total parts of the alloy.
question_patterns: Calculate the percentage of gold in 22 carat gold.
What is the purity of 18 carat gold?
How much alloy is present in 20 carat gold?
Find the gold content in a 24 carat sample.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the given carat value by the standard 24 carats.
Multiply the ratio by 100 to get the purity percentage.

concepts.title: Alloying and Amalgams
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, Creating a homogeneous mixture of a metal with other elements to enhance properties like hardness or corrosion resistance.
concepts.key_idea: Alloying changes pure metal properties; amalgams specifically contain mercury.
question_patterns: What is an alloy?
Define an amalgam.
What are the constituents of stainless steel?
Why is pure iron not used for construction?
Name the components of brass and bronze.

solution_steps.explain: List the primary metal and the added elements.
If mercury is present, classify the alloy as an amalgam.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Predict the reaction when an iron nail is placed in {solution}.

solution_template.explain: Iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series.
Iron displaces copper, forming iron sulphate and a brown copper coating.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the percentage of pure gold in {carat} carat gold.

solution_template.explain: Ratio of gold is 22 parts out of 24.
